penetration_assumption: EXPLICIT: I did NOT assume a share of the 4,700 residents. Every comparable line in ARY's own health shelf reaches between 30 and 522 bills a year out of 372,320 (VERIFIED 12m: Dettol Bandaid 300 bills/Rs 4,457; Cotton Buds 522/Rs 14,860; Strepsils 216/Rs 7,325; Vicks VapoRub 10ml 210/Rs 9,900; Boroline 179/Rs 8,910; Cipla ORS RTD 184/Rs 8,161; Savlon 50ml 96/Rs 3,282; Hot Water Bag 33/Rs 10,240). I assume each newly added line lands INSIDE that observed band (35-220 bills/yr, i.e. 0.01%-0.06% of transactions) at the pack price the demand research gives. Worked example: adhesive-bandage packs = 150 bills/yr x Rs 95 = Rs 14,250; ORS sachets = 220 bills/yr x Rs 40 = Rs 8,800; crepe bandage = 55 bills/yr x Rs 260 = Rs 14,300. Total Rs 1,04,100 gross (GST-inclusive). This is ESTIMATED, not verified. It deliberately assumes NO growth in the underlying health-shelf demand, because the shelf is only 1.29% of bills and Akal Hospital dispenses on the same campus. MARGIN: Rs 73,600 of the total is unbranded surgical (bandage/gauze/crepe/tape/cotton/spirit/kit/thermometer) at 12% GST and 32% net GM, anchored on VERIFIED Dettol Bandaid 40.1%, Strepsils 34.1%, Vicks Inhaler 31.8%; Rs 30,500 is branded (ORS, povidone-iodine, calamine, Burnol, Odomos) at 5% GST and 18% net GM, anchored on VERIFIED Savlon 22.9%, Moov 16.4%, Boroline 11.8%, Eno 13.4%. Gross profit Rs 26,257, which I round to Rs 26,300.
probe_evidence: Every "absent" claim was re-tested with 6-15 word variants across ALL 21,479 SKUs (not just the Medicare group), because probe's OR-substring matching over-captures (e.g. "eno" hits "Jalapeno" and "Senorita"; "lice" hits "Amul Cheese Slices"; "probiotic" hits "Amul Chocobar Probiotic" ice cream; "pudin" hits Vim Bar Pudina). ZERO SKUs returned for: antacid (digene/gelusil/polycrol/diovol/mucaine/acidity/rantac/aciloc/omez/pantop/pantocid/zinetac/gaviscon); antihistamine (cetiri/cetzine/cetrizine/citrizine/alerid/okacet/levocet/xyzal/allegra/avil/montek/allergy); laxative (dulcoflex/dulcolax/bisacodyl/laxative/cremaffin/duphalac/lactulose/looz/constipation); povidone (betadine/povidone/cipladine/wokadine/tincture); calamine+burn (calamine/caladryl/burnol/silverex/sulphadiazine/soframycin/neosporin/mupirocin); ORS sachet (electral/walyte/prolyte/oral rehydration/ors powder); gargle (betadine/hexidine/gargle/zytee/tantum/chlorhexidine); surgical spirit (surgical spirit/hydrogen peroxide/peroxide); ear drops; first-aid kit (first aid kit/firstaid/medical kit/emergency kit). WOUND DRESSING: 12 terms (gauze/guaze/bandage/bandaid/hansaplast/handyplast/micropore/zinc oxide tape/medical tape/dressing pad/wound) return exactly ONE SKU in the whole catalogue - 01S8 Dettol Bandaid, 1,824 units / 300 bills / Rs 4,457, sold loose at Rs 2.44. ANALGESIC: 15 terms return 7 SKUs, of which 3 sold anything in 12 months - Disprin Rs 907, Paracitamol 500 Rs 590, Crocin 500 Rs 502 = Rs 1,999 total for ~4,700 people. Correct spelling "paracetamol" returns ZERO; ARY spells it "Paracitamol" (spelling trap). No 650mg exists. THERMOMETER: 3 SKUs (Hicks, Cipla x2), all listed, all zero sales, all zero stock. Broad sweep on " tab"/tablet/capsule/syrup/" mg" across all 21,479 SKUs returns only chocolate syrup, woolen caps, Fevikwik 500 Mg and table fans beyond the Medicare group - there is no hidden pharmacy section anywhere in this database.

blockers: LICENCE - blocks the majority of the research's rupees. No Form 20/21 retail drug licence is evidenced and all 11 suppliers of the Medicare group are general FMCG wholesalers (Baghat Enterprises, Himachal Wholesale Syndicate, Anchal Trading, Nirman Associates, Solan Agencies) - not one pharmaceutical distributor. This blocks paracetamol 650, ibuprofen/Combiflam, cetirizine, Digene/Gelusil, Pantocid/Omez/Rantac, Dulcoflex, eye drops and ear drops. SEPARATE COMPLIANCE FLAG for a human: ARY already lists and has sold Crocin 500, Disprin, Avomine, Otrivin nasal spray, Wincold and D-Cold Total - that is an exposure to check, not an asset to build on.

CAMPUS DISPENSARY - Akal Hospital (AccountID 244) is on the same campus and is ARY's own credit customer, billed at the Ary Baru Sahib counter: 60 bills / Rs 78,210 in 12 months, all bedsheets, curtains, room heaters, quilts and Vaseline, zero medicines. A charitable hospital dispensing to residents is the most credible explanation for Rs 1,999 of annual analgesic sales among ~4,700 people. NOT CHECKED and needs a human: does the hospital dispense free or subsidised to campus residents? If yes, even my first-aid estimate is optimistic; if no, ORS and dressings could run 2x.

SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH HP - no surgical-dressings distributor exists in the purchase ledger. The branded half (Hansaplast, Betadine, Burnol, Electral, Odomos, thermometer) can come from the existing FMCG wholesalers; the unbranded half (gauze, crepe, micropore tape, cotton roll) needs a new supplier relationship, most likely from Solan or Nahan. That is why effort is weeks, not days.
EXPIRY WRITE-OFF - dressings and ORS run 24-36 month shelf life at 35-220 units a year per line. A standard case pack can outlive its date. Buy the smallest case pack; do not take a scheme quantity.

CAPITAL IS NOT THE BLOCKER, BUYING DISCIPLINE IS - the 172 dormant health SKUs tie up 7 units and Rs 986 in total, so delisting them frees nothing. The same buying trip should restock the 35 proven sellers that are at ZERO on-hand today (Rs 79,255 of 12m sales, dark 156 days on average, including Dabur Honitus out 64 days and Boroline out 182 days). That recovers an estimated Rs 58,158/yr with no new listing, no new supplier and no licence - more than half the entire add opportunity, and it should be done FIRST.

MARGIN IS THINNER THAN THE RESEARCH ASSUMED - the health shelf's VERIFIED weighted gross margin, net of GST on both sides and costed off PurchaseDetail, is 16.96% (Rs 2,78,369 net sales vs Rs 2,31,157 net COGS across 87 SKUs). The demand research's 20-35% bands overstate profit by roughly 40%. Only the unbranded surgical lines clear 30%.
kill_reason: NOT a kill - the assortment gap is real and is in fact WIDER than the coverage diff reported - but it is worth Rs 1.04 lakh a year, not the crore-scale number the research fleet's raw recommendations imply, and availability is the larger lever inside the same category. Three reasons the number is small, all VERIFIED live on 2026-08-30 over the window 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31. (1) THE DIFF IS FICTION: 28.8% "coverage" rests on substring hits - "pan" was credited with Rs 10.73 L of PPI coverage, "200" with Rs 19.79 L of osmotic laxative, "insta" with WHO ORS, "shikanji" with ORS 4.4g, "fruit" with paediatric paracetamol, "gold" with clotrimazole cream, "probiotic" with Amul Chocobar Probiotic ICE CREAM. Re-probed with 6-15 variants each, 18+ lines the diff called covered have ZERO SKU in all 21,479 products. (2) THE DEMAND IS NOT AT ARY: a full 12 months of oral analgesics for ~4,700 residents is Disprin Rs 907 + Paracitamol 500 Rs 590 + Crocin 500 Rs 502 = Rs 1,999. The whole Medicare group is Rs 3,23,292 = 0.42% of Rs 7,66,85,036 turnover, appearing on 4,813 of 372,320 bills = 1.29% attach, Rs 69 per resident per year. Akal Hospital is on the same campus, is ARY's own credit customer, and buys bedsheets not medicines. (3) AVAILABILITY DOMINATES: of 272 health SKUs, 107 have NEVER sold once and 65 more went dark - 171 of those 172 carry zero stock and Rs 986 of capital combined, so delisting frees nothing; meanwhile 35 SKUs that DO sell sit at ZERO on-hand today with Rs 79,255 of proven 12m demand, dark 156 days on average (Dabur Honitus, the shelf's #2 line at Rs 16,452, out 64 days; Boroline out 182 days; Moov 20g out 124 days; Vicks VapoRub 10ml down to 0.3 months cover entering cough season). Restocking those is worth an estimated Rs 58,158/yr and requires no listing decision at all. RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE: restock the 35 first, add the 13 licence-free first-aid lines second, and do not touch anything requiring a drug licence until a human answers whether Akal Hospital already dispenses to residents.
